required_outcomes: Separates the report into two issues needing different trades: the front (and back) door and frame, which must be slammed and put the glass at risk, and the new fridge freezer that is still not cooling a day after it was fitted.

Handles the fridge freezer as an urgent appliance fault on a brand-new installation: goes back to the fitter or supplier under the installation or manufacturer warranty and tells the landlord; the unanswered make-and-model question is now relevant, and the tenant has already said both compartments are affected.

Handles the doors as a doors/security job above routine (main entrance, glass at risk), seeking landlord approval for a joiner or door specialist with the fault described, and gives the tenant a safety note not to slam the glazed door.
Acknowledges the tenant on both issues without promising dates nobody has confirmed.
acceptable_alternatives: Keeping one request but recording both issues with separate actions and trades, as long as neither is dropped.
Asking the tenant to check the temperature setting and that the appliance is not in a demo or holiday mode, provided the fitter or supplier is still contacted.
positive_behaviours: Includes the back door, which the tenant says has the same problem, in the door request.
Advises the tenant to keep food out of the fridge freezer until it holds temperature.
red_flags: Handling only the fridge (the intake category) and dropping the doors, or only the doors and dropping the fridge.
Treating the fridge freezer as a fresh chargeable repair rather than a warranty or installation return on a new appliance.
prohibited_actions: Sending an appliance engineer to the door, or a joiner to the fridge freezer.
Assigning a door contractor before the landlord has approved, when nothing says the door cannot be secured.
critical_failures: Leaving one of the two faults with no action at all.
